heading: Know who is responsible
intro: Ask for the operator’s name and the guiding arrangements for your actual booking. Distinguish the company selling the trip from the provider delivering it. Confirm qualifications relevant to the planned activities and who takes responsibility for transport. Staffing can change, so ask how substitutions are communicated rather than demand a promise that one named team can never change.
points: Confirm the operator delivering each part of the trip.
Ask about guiding qualifications for the planned activities.
Ask how staffing changes are communicated.

heading: Review the whole route
intro: Keep a route description that includes arrival towns, meeting points, road segments, river transfers and the base itself. Compare it with current official advice before confirming travel. Ask the provider what would change or cancel an outing. A useful itinerary identifies responsibilities and locations; a very detailed timetable does not establish the conditions you will encounter.
points: Ask for the actual gateway and transfer route.
Ask what conditions would change the program.
Confirm how route changes are communicated.

heading: Clarify transport responsibilities
intro: Treat each transport segment as part of the review, including any journey you arrange independently. Identify the responsible provider, agreed meeting instructions and arrangements for luggage. Ask about the activity-specific equipment and briefing before boarding. Clarify what happens during delays or a missed meeting. Do not assume that a package description transfers responsibility for every connection to one operator.
points: Identify who manages each transfer and connection.
Ask how bags travel when the vehicle or boat changes.
Clarify the arrangements for delays and missed meetings.

heading: Understand the response plan
intro: Ask for a practical explanation of how an urgent message reaches help from the base and from outings. Clarify the responsible contact and the alternatives when usual communication is unavailable. Ask how onward assistance is arranged and what limitations affect it. Focus on the usable plan; a device name, technical specification or precise-looking time estimate is not proof that assistance can reach every location.
points: Ask who receives urgent messages from each outing.
Ask what happens when normal communication is unavailable.
Clarify onward assistance and the plan’s limitations.

heading: Match the activity to your needs
intro: Ask what the planned activity requires in walking, boarding, balance or time away from the base. Describe relevant practical needs to the provider privately. Confirm the equipment supplied, sizes and instructions, and any available alternatives. Keep personal health decisions with a qualified clinician. A generic packing list or a photograph of another group cannot establish whether the program meets your requirements.
points: List personal items separately from supplied equipment.
Ask about requirements for each planned activity.
Confirm the alternatives before accepting the program.

heading: Keep the change terms
intro: Review written cancellation and change terms alongside the itinerary. Identify deadlines, charges and what happens if a provider cancels or changes a route. Ask how a delayed arrival affects the program and who you contact. Use the terms for the actual booking rather than assume a universal cutoff or refund. Keep those records accessible with the confirmed contact details.
points: Request the actual cancellation deadlines and charges.
Ask what happens when conditions change the itinerary.
Confirm the contact and process for a delayed arrival.
